name: harness-edit-loop-study-v1
description: Narrow first-version study of self-improving agent harnesses (after Weng 2026 / STOP / ADAS / AFlow / Self-Harness). One falsifiable question only: on a FIXED small task suite with a FIXED base model, does a bounded propose-validate-accept harness-edit loop (verifier-grounded weakness mining -> single-surface bounded edit -> held-in AND held-out non-regression gate) measurably improve task pass rate over a frozen harness, and which single editable surface (context-management logic vs tool-invocation policy vs workflow control flow) yields the largest verified gain? Negative and null results are in scope and count as outcomes.

constraints.fixed_base_model: exactly one open-weights model per experiment; model identity recorded in the plan
constraints.fixed_task_suite: exactly one small, fixed task suite per experiment; no suite switching mid-experiment
constraints.single_editable_surface: each experiment varies ONE harness surface only; joint-surface search is out of scope for v1
constraints.acceptance_rule: an edit is accepted only with no regression on held-in AND held-out splits; the split must be defined in the plan before any run
constraints.written_prediction_required: every experiment states its predicted direction and magnitude before execution
constraints.negative_results_in_scope: a null or negative result with a clean split is a valid, reportable outcome

out_of_scope: modifying the production DeepGraph harness or any live system (that is the supervised domain of the self-improving-harness agenda)
unbounded or open-ended self-modification loops without a regression gate
experiments without a pre-registered held-in/held-out split
